benefits.label: Why skills
title: Repeat the work,
not the explanation.
benefits.description: Skills reuse stable instructions and hand predictable procedures to scripts, so the model can focus on decisions that need context.

items.label: Reusable instructions
items.title: Stop rebuilding the same instructions.
items.description: Write the sequence, examples, and safety rules once in SKILL.md. Repeated requests can reuse the same prefix, making prompt caching easier to use on models that support it.

items.label: Deterministic scripts
items.title: Let scripts handle predictable work.
items.description: Use scripts for steps with clear outcomes, such as file discovery, format checks, and data synchronization. The model no longer has to work through the same procedure every time.

items.label: Focused judgment
items.title: Keep the LLM focused on judgment.
items.description: Use the model for requirements, code review, and risk decisions that need context. Record the execution order and completion criteria in the skill.

tagline.label: Repeatable by design

faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.description: What to know before you install.

items.question: What exactly is a skill?
items.answer: A skill is a SKILL.md document that defines how an agent should perform a specific task. It includes the execution sequence, safety rules, and output format so repeated requests follow the same standard.

items.question: How is it different from a regular prompt?
items.answer: A prompt disappears when the conversation ends, but a skill remains as a file. You can version it, share it with a team, and call it again by name, such as $review-me.

items.question: Do skills always reduce token usage?
items.answer: No—savings are not guaranteed. Prompt caching depends on the model, instruction length, and whether the same prefix is preserved. Skills are designed to reuse stable instructions and separate scripted steps, which can reduce unnecessary LLM work.

items.question: Which tasks should scripts handle?
items.answer: Tasks whose inputs and outputs can be checked by rules. Scripts handle file discovery, format validation, catalog synchronization, and test execution; the LLM handles interpretation and review.

items.question: Which agents can use these skills?
items.answer: Claude Code and Codex are supported by default. Codex calls the same SKILL.md with $name, while Claude Code uses /name. The installer also supports agents such as Gemini CLI and GitHub Copilot CLI.

items.question: What gets added to my computer?
items.answer: npx skills add downloads the repository and links each agent to the same source. The source stays in one place, and removing the links cleanly uninstalls the skills.

items.question: Can a skill commit or push on its own?
items.answer: Each skill states its safety rules explicitly. For example, Git skills use explicit staging only, forbid force pushes, and stop to report when a push is rejected.

items.question: Can I install only selected skills?
items.answer: Yes. Replace --skill '*' in the install command with the name of the skill you want. Each skill README also includes its individual install command.

items.question: How do I update installed skills?
items.answer: Run npx skills update chann/skills to update installed skills to the latest version.

items.question: Are there fees or license restrictions?
items.answer: No. The entire repository is open source under the MIT License. You can fork it and adapt the skills to your team’s rules.

review-me.summary: Review every important choice in a plan or design so nothing is left unresolved.
review-me.whenToUse: Before implementation, when ambiguous choices, boundaries, and failure or recovery conditions must be resolved
review-me.result: Resolved choices, completion criteria for each one, acceptance examples, and an explicit deferral list

code-review.summary: Find defects and risks in code changes and produce a bilingual report.
code-review.whenToUse: When reviewing a PR, commit, branch, or working tree before release
code-review.result: A Markdown review and a standalone HTML review

code-review-md.summary: Save a code review as Markdown only, without browser output.
code-review-md.whenToUse: When a review must be posted to a PR comment or documentation pipeline

diff-summary.summary: Explain a change’s purpose, behavior, structure, and test impact with evidence.
diff-summary.whenToUse: When you need to understand quickly why code changed
diff-summary.result: Korean and English Markdown plus an interactive HTML summary

diff-summary-md.summary: Save the same change explanation as Markdown only, without HTML.
diff-summary-md.whenToUse: When a change summary needs to go directly into repository docs or an issue

diff-summary-quiz.summary: Add an interactive comprehension quiz to a change summary.
diff-summary-quiz.whenToUse: For onboarding, review training, or validating a change handoff
diff-summary-quiz.result: A bilingual summary and a quiz with answers

diff-viewer.summary: Render the current Git diff as a readable standalone HTML page.
diff-viewer.whenToUse: When you want to inspect the raw patch in a browser without analysis
diff-viewer.result: A unified or split-view HTML diff

bug-hunt.summary: Reproduce first, falsify hypotheses in a ledger, and pin the fix with a check that failed first.
bug-hunt.whenToUse: When a bug's cause is not obvious, a test fails intermittently, or something suddenly got slower
bug-hunt.result: A recorded reproduction, a falsification ledger, a failing-first check, and a record under .bug-hunts/

research-brief.summary: Answer a technical question from primary sources, with every claim tiered and version-pinned.
research-brief.whenToUse: When behavior or a specification must be confirmed against official sources you can check again later
research-brief.result: A bottom-line answer with confidence, a tiered claim table, a contradiction ledger, and open questions

gen-docs.summary: Create or update core project docs while preserving existing wording.
gen-docs.whenToUse: When README, architecture, or usage docs have drifted from the code

plan-summary.summary: Summarize explicit plans, PRDs, specifications, and designs in matching Korean and English reports.
plan-summary.whenToUse: When a team needs the goals, scope, decisions, dependencies, risks, and open questions from selected documents
plan-summary.result: Korean and English PS-* Markdown cards plus one self-contained bilingual HTML report

plan-summary-md.summary: Write the matching Korean and English plan summaries as Markdown only.
plan-summary-md.whenToUse: When a plan summary belongs in repository docs, an issue, or another text-only workflow
plan-summary-md.result: Two validated Markdown reports under .plan-summaries/ with no HTML or browser open

plan-summary-quiz.summary: Add a corresponding comprehension quiz to a bilingual plan summary.
plan-summary-quiz.whenToUse: For onboarding, plan handoffs, or checking understanding of requirements and design decisions
plan-summary-quiz.result: Bilingual PS-* summaries and corresponding QZ-* questions in Markdown and interactive offline HTML

human-friendly-writing.summary: Rewrite AI-written Korean text into natural, human-sounding prose without changing its meaning.
human-friendly-writing.whenToUse: When Korean text reads AI-flavored — English concept words like contract, envelope, or parity calqued literally, or translation-ese rhythm
human-friendly-writing.result: The rewritten Korean text plus a short plain-language note on what changed

git-commit.summary: Split working-tree changes into logical Conventional Commit units.
git-commit.whenToUse: When mixed changes need to become reviewable commits
git-commit.result: One or more explicitly staged commits

git-commit-push.summary: Create logical commits, then publish them with a normal push.
git-commit-push.whenToUse: When completed work should be organized and published in one pass
git-commit-push.result: Conventional Commits and a remote push

git-commit-push-realtime.summary: Commit and push each verified result as soon as it is complete.
git-commit-push-realtime.whenToUse: When a long implementation should leave reviewable checkpoints on the remote
git-commit-push-realtime.result: Verified checkpoints with remote publication confirmed every time

git-commit-realtime.summary: Create a local commit for each verified result and leave pushing for later.
git-commit-realtime.whenToUse: When the work history should be preserved but publication timing remains manual
git-commit-realtime.result: Local checkpoints that do not touch the remote

git-commit-rewrite.summary: Rewrite recent commit titles in Conventional Commit format.
git-commit-rewrite.whenToUse: When existing commit messages need a consistent structure
git-commit-rewrite.result: A consistent commit history after safety checks

git-merge-to-main.summary: Merge the current branch into main safely and clean up the source branch.
git-merge-to-main.whenToUse: When integrating a feature branch into main
git-merge-to-main.result: A verified main merge and safe branch deletion

git-merge-to-dev.summary: Merge the current branch into dev or develop and clean it up safely.
git-merge-to-dev.whenToUse: When integrating a feature branch into the development branch
git-merge-to-dev.result: A verified dev merge and safe branch deletion

git-branch-cleanup.summary: Safely delete only local branches already merged into a protected branch.
git-branch-cleanup.whenToUse: When accumulated local branches need risk-free cleanup
git-branch-cleanup.result: Cleanup limited to merged branches eligible for safe delete

gen-frontend-handoff.summary: Turn backend changes into the context needed for frontend and client work.
gen-frontend-handoff.whenToUse: When handing API changes to web, mobile, or SDK developers
gen-frontend-handoff.result: A frontend handoff covering the API contract, UI states, errors, and verification

gen-backend-handoff.summary: Document API and data changes for the server work that follows.
gen-backend-handoff.whenToUse: When handing backend implementation or operations work to another developer
gen-backend-handoff.result: A backend handoff covering APIs, databases, jobs, and rollout

long-task.summary: Run a large project end to end through milestones and verification cycles.
long-task.whenToUse: When delegating an autonomous implementation that will take several hours
long-task.result: An execution record covering planning, parallel work, review, and completion checks

build-reinstall.summary: Build the current project, reinstall it with project-owned commands, and verify that the installed result matches the new build.
build-reinstall.whenToUse: After code work is complete and a local app or CLI must be replaced with the new build
build-reinstall.result: Build, reinstall, smoke-check, and SHA-256 installed-artifact evidence

skill-forge.summary: Author a skill package against the contract and publish every surface it needs.
skill-forge.whenToUse: When adding, renaming, or repairing a skill so it follows the same rules as the rest
skill-forge.result: SKILL.md, Codex descriptor, slash command, evals, catalog, four locales, counts, and tests

skill-audit.summary: Check every packaged skill against the nine contract rules and report what fails.
skill-audit.whenToUse: Before a merge or release, to confirm packages and the catalog have not drifted apart
skill-audit.result: A violation list naming rule, skill, and file, plus a non-zero exit code

work-summary.summary: Create a date-range work report from local coding-agent history.
work-summary.whenToUse: When summarizing requests and work completed today, this week, this month, or another period
work-summary.result: A concise or detailed Markdown work report, optionally under .work-summaries/
